summary: F2 confirms one suspicious non-interactive sign-in from Turkcell (TR) outside the account baseline using valid credentials (T1078.004). F3 indicates most sign-ins come from Portugal via university VPN vpn-edge-02 on device LT-3104. Rejected impossible-travel, password-spray, and KEV appliance claims because the TR event is a mail-sync token, PT sign-ins are VPN-mediated, failures are background noise, and appliance firmware includes fixes. Evidence shows partial access signals without confirmed abuse, but policy mandates escalation.

risk.rationale: All asserted attack narratives are rejected by the provided critics and there are no data-quality conflicts. F2 (CONFIRMED 0.75) records a single Turkcell (TR) sign-in outside baseline tagged T1078.004, but the impossible-travel claim is rebutted: that TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the account holder, and the user's actual sign-ins (F3, LIKELY 0.5, PT, 10 events) come through the university VPN vpn-edge-02 from known device LT-3104. The password-spray claim fails (193.140.10.21 is shared egress with 201 MFA completions in 30 days; failures are background noise). The VPN KEV claims are not relevant/exposure: vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8 includes the cited fixes, and vpn-edge-01 never carried a sign-in for this account. No confirmed account-takeover chain exists (not contain); no weak unexplained signal remains (not monitor); no conflicting/insufficient evidence requiring a human (not escalate). The confirmed finding F2 is cited to satisfy the override requirement for departing from a stricter call.
